items.name: Basel 3.1 (UK)
items.stage: Final rules published (PS1/26, Jan 2026) — implementation 1 Jan 2027, transitional period to end-2030
items.eclImpact: Removes the Pillar 1 SME support factor, offset by a firm-specific SME lending adjustment in Pillar 2A, and introduces a 45% risk weight for retail SME transactors. Changes the capital cost of BB lending and interacts with IFRS 9 provisioning via the output floor and expected-loss capital deductions.

source.title: Norton Rose Fulbright, Global Regulation Tomorrow — Implementation of Basel 3.1: PRA publishes final rules

items.name: Ring-fencing reform
items.stage: HMT review conclusions published 18 May 2026 — deposit threshold raised £25bn to £35bn; PRA consulting summer 2026 on shared services; growth allowance up to 10% of credit RWAs proposed
items.eclImpact: Reshapes which entity books BB exposure and how group capital/MREL is calibrated (RFB internal MREL scalar review in H2 2026). A growth allowance letting RFBs take otherwise-prohibited exposures could alter the risk mix behind the BB ECL stack.

source.title: HM Treasury — Safeguarding Stability, Enabling Growth: The Ring-Fencing Review

items.name: Companies House reform (ECCTA)
items.stage: Mandatory identity verification for new directors/PSCs live since 18 Nov 2025; existing directors must verify by autumn 2026; accounts reform (small-company P&L filing, software-only) phased to 2027
items.eclImpact: Small-company P&L filing ends abridged/filleted accounts, materially improving financial data available for BB credit assessment and PD modelling of micro-SMEs. IDV cleans the register that KYC, fraud screening and early-warning tools depend on.

source.title: ICAEW — Timeline for Companies House ID changes

items.name: APP fraud reimbursement review
items.stage: Independent evaluation published 1 Jul 2026 (losses down ~£73m/yr, 97% reimbursement); formal consultation on £85k cap and 50/50 PSP split due December 2026
items.eclImpact: Reimbursement liability sits with sending/receiving PSPs, creating a non-credit loss line that competes with impairment for P&L attention; any cap recalibration changes fraud-loss provisioning for business payment fraud on BB accounts.

source.title: Global Regulation Tomorrow — Payment fraud falls by £73m following PSR reimbursement scheme

items.name: Commercial VRPs (open banking payments)
items.stage: UKPI cVRP scheme went live 2 Jun 2026 (Wave 1: utilities, financial services, government); Wave 2 e-commerce expected end-2026; FCA to fold lessons into long-term framework
items.eclImpact: cVRP-enabled sweeping and payments erode BCA transaction data primacy — the richest early-warning input for BB SICR triggers. Longer-term, open banking rails support cash-flow-based underwriting that could reshape PD data sources.

source.title: PSR/FCA — Commercial variable recurring payments: update on delivery (Dec 2025)

items.name: Bank Referral Scheme & CCDS reform
items.stage: HMT response 11 May 2026: no BRS legislation — industry-led improvement proposals due to HMT by 18 Dec 2026; CCDS to be expanded by legislation beyond banks
items.eclImpact: Expanded commercial credit data sharing widens the bureau data behind SME PD models and improves visibility of borrower leverage across lenders — a data-quality upgrade for ECL and affordability assessment.

source.title: HM Treasury — Government response: Commercial Credit Data Sharing and Bank Referral Scheme

items.name: Growth Guarantee Scheme extension
items.stage: Extended in 2025 Spending Review to 31 March 2030; 70% guarantee, terms unchanged; RLS3/GGS performance data published quarterly
items.eclImpact: Keeps a 70% government guarantee available on eligible BB new-lend to 2030, structurally lowering LGD on covered facilities and cushioning risk appetite through the Basel 3.1 capital transition.

source.title: British Business Bank — Growth Guarantee Scheme (GGS)

items.name: FCA SME access-to-finance work
items.stage: Call for Input closed (issued 18 Mar 2026); stakeholder roundtables held May 2026; summary of insights and next steps due later in 2026
items.eclImpact: Could extend conduct expectations further into (largely unregulated) SME lending; any push on lending criteria, forbearance treatment or declined-application transparency would touch BB collections and staging practice.

source.title: FCA — Understanding how our regulation can help SMEs access finance (Call for Input)

items.name: PRA IFRS 9 ECL expectations (Dear CFO)
items.stage: Latest thematic Dear CFO letter (2025): model risk elevated, PMA completeness and LGD recovery-assumption realism under scrutiny; annual thematic cycle continues into 2026
items.eclImpact: Direct supervisory pressure on BB ECL practice: challenge model responsiveness to current credit-risk drivers, evidence PMAs, and de-bias LGD for vulnerable sectors — expect these themes in year-end audit and PRA engagement.

source.title: Bank of England PRA — Thematic feedback on accounting for IFRS 9 expected credit losses (Dear CFO letter)

items.name: FCA Open Finance Roadmap
items.stage: Roadmap published April 2026 — SME lending and mortgages named first priority use cases; TechSprints ran Nov 2025-Feb 2026; full regulatory framework targeted by end-2027
items.eclImpact: Open finance data-sharing for SME credit would broaden the cash-flow and account data available for underwriting and monitoring — over time a richer SICR/early-warning toolkit, and lower information advantage for incumbent BCA banks.

source.title: Global Regulation Tomorrow — FCA publishes Open Finance Roadmap
